arlington.angle: Small-city practicality: ramblers, farmhouse remodels, well water and iron staining; hard-working bathrooms redone once and done right.

bothell.angle: 90s-boom subdivisions hitting the age where builder-grade tub surrounds fail; first-remodel families comparing bids.

cottage-lake.angle: Wooded acreage homes, private wells, mudroom and entry tile that has to survive boots, dogs and gravel driveways.

duvall.angle: Valley weather and long wet winters; heated floors as morning comfort in farmhouse and new-build baths alike.

edmonds.angle: View homes and mid-century baths near the ferry; owners upgrading original 60s tile without losing character.

everett.angle: Working-city housing stock from 1910s craftsman to 90s split-levels; honest triage between repair and full re-tile.

issaquah.angle: Newer Highlands construction vs older in-town homes; large-format porcelain and curbless showers in recent remodels.

kenmore.region: the north end of Lake Washington
kenmore.angle: Lakeside humidity and split-level baths; ventilation and waterproofing as the quiet heroes of a remodel.

kirkland.angle: Condo and view-home remodels where design ambition meets HOA logistics; zellige and designer porcelain requests.

lake-stevens.angle: Fast-growing families, new construction punch-lists and first big bathroom upgrades; budget clarity above all.

lynnwood.angle: 70s–80s ramblers mid-renovation; replacing acrylic surrounds with real tiled showers before resale.

marysville.angle: Value-focused big-box tile purchases installed properly; what $3 tile needs underneath it to last.

medina.region: the Gold Coast of Lake Washington
medina.angle: High-end stone, slab-look porcelain and steam showers; discretion, protection of finishes, exacting layout.

mercer-island.angle: Mid-century daylight ramblers with original baths; structural honesty about 60-year-old subfloors before tile goes down.

mill-creek.angle: Planned-community homes turning 30; ensuite master baths refreshed with heated floors and niche storage.

monroe.angle: Acreage and shop-house properties; durable porcelain for entries and utility spaces plus one showpiece bath.

mukilteo.angle: Salt air, ferry-town view homes, and baths remodeled around a view window; condensation-aware assemblies.

newcastle.angle: 90s luxury builds where beige 4x4 tile dates a great house; full-bath transformations with large format.

north-bend.angle: Mountain weather, mudrooms, wood stoves and radiant-heated tile as a genuine comfort feature at elevation.

oak-harbor.angle: Navy-family timelines and island logistics; scheduling certainty, materials ordered right the first time.

redmond.angle: Data-driven homeowners who want the assembly spec explained; smart thermostats on heated floors.

renton.angle: Boeing-era ramblers and newer hillside townhomes; two very different substrates, one waterproofing standard.

sammamish.angle: Family homes with double-vanity ensuites; kid-proof floors, ledger-stone fireplaces, weekend-proof grout.

seattle.angle: Craftsman and townhome baths from Ballard to Beacon Hill; old-house framing surprises handled without drama.

shoreline.angle: Post-war brick ramblers with tiny baths; layouts that make 5x8 feet feel bigger with the right format.

snohomish.angle: Historic-district Victorians and farm properties; period-appropriate tile with modern waterproofing hidden behind it.

snoqualmie.angle: Ridge new-builds coming off warranty; fixing builder shortcuts before they become leaks.

whidbey-island.angle: Island homes, beach cabins and ferry-scheduled projects; moisture everywhere, planning that respects the boat.

woodinville.angle: Entertaining kitchens and tasting-room-inspired backsplashes; hosting-ready durability.
